deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues a magnetometer damping run in the induction papers. The previous page is dated April 15 at the Sternwarte, 8.9 °C, headed 'Phys. 4'. The next page is dated 1836 March 21 and gives a period of 42.60 s. The data are amplitudes (arcs, in scale divisions) of a freely swinging magnetometer magnet, taken in blocks of four consecutive oscillations. This page carries the run from oscillation 90 to 148 and closes with a thermometer reading of 9.7 °C.

(1) Data per block. Each block gives the oscillation numbers n, the clock time of the first oscillation, the arcs A_n and their common logarithms log10 A_n. Example: log10 525.65 = 2.72070.

(2) Block means. Gauss averages the four logarithms. He writes the result in the form 2.71757.25, meaning 2.7175725 (log A at the block centre, e.g. n = 91.5).
- 90–93: 10.87029/4 = 2.7175725
- 100–103: 2.69636
- 105–108: 2.67233
- 115–118: 2.5978625
- 120–123: 2.57411
- 130–133: 2.552265
- 135–138: 2.5279375
- 145–148: 2.4525275

(3) Times. Consecutive blocks are 10 or 5 oscillations apart. The times differ by 7'06" = 426 s and 3'33" = 213 s, so T ≈ 42.6 s, agreeing with 42"60 on the next page. Examples: 10h0'43" → 7'49" → 11'22" → 18'28" → 22'0" → 29'7" → 32'41" → 39'47". Counting from 8h57'31" for n = 1 gives T ≈ 3792/89 ≈ 42.607 s.

(4) Implicit step (mine). The blocks form pairs: (90,100), (105,115), (120,130), (135,145), and on the previous page (1,11), (16,26), and so on. Dividing the difference of the block means by 10 gives the logarithmic decrement per oscillation, λ = [mean(n) − mean(n+10)]/10:
- 90→100: 0.002121
- 105→115: 0.007447
- 120→130: 0.002185
- 135→145: 0.007541
Within-block slopes agree: about 0.0021 per oscillation versus about 0.0074. The damping therefore alternates between a weak value and a strong one (about 3.5× larger). This is most plausibly open versus closed multiplier circuit, i.e. damping by induced currents, consistent with the bundle title 'Induktion'.

(5) Bottom table. Each pair of blocks has a midpoint index: (1+14)/2 = 7½, (16+29)/2 = 22½, …, (135+148)/2 = 141½. Against each Gauss lists a scale value: 187.25, 714.70, 193.875, 725.9, 201.525, 746.025, 212.125, 744.675, 218.450, 754.100. The same values are written between the block pairs on the two pages. They alternate between about 190–218 and about 714–754, a jump of roughly 530 divisions. The strongly damped pairs go with the high values. They are evidently rest or deflection positions (each slowly drifting upward). The next page tabulates such alternating readings and their differences (≈ 521–531).

Purpose: to determine the logarithmic decrement of the magnet's swings under two alternating conditions, and the associated positions. In other words, to measure how strongly the induced currents damp the needle.
errors: No error in any of the eight block means; all check exactly against the listed logarithms.

Several five-place logarithms are one unit off in the last place: log10(290.85) = 2.463669 (Gauss 2.46366), log10(285.85) = 2.456138 (Gauss 2.45613), log10(328.55) = 2.516602 (Gauss 2.51661). These are interpolation slips from tables and are immaterial.
Times are rounded to the second: computed 22'01", 29'06", 32'40" against written 22'0", 29'7", 32'41". These are either rounding or observed times; no real error.

results.what: Logarithmic decrement of a damped magnetometer from block-averaged log amplitudes, compared between two alternating circuit conditions (weak ≈ 0.0021 vs strong ≈ 0.0074 per oscillation).
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement; electromagnetic (eddy/induced-current) damping of a galvanometer/magnetometer
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (decrement treatment in Intensitas, 1832/33) and Wilhelm Weber (induction damping, 'Dämpfer', c. 1837–38, Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins)

results.what: Period of the magnetometer from timed oscillation counts (T ≈ 42.6 s).
Alternating rest/deflection positions assigned to the midpoint indices of block pairs.
results.modern_name: Equilibrium-point determination of a swinging needle

deep.surprise_reason: Routine laboratory reduction from the Gauss–Weber magnetic/induction experiments of 1836: logarithms of amplitudes, block means and implied decrements. The topic of induction damping is known Göttingen work; the page contains no new mathematics.
